title: Follow-up: one argument scanner for --repo, and ADR 0002's produces nit
description: LOW from the approved review of opum-ai/glyph-cli#34 at f1942deb. The argv pre-scans in src/program.ts and commander disagree on --repo's value: `glyph --repo --json callers x` prints text on success but a JSON envelope on failure, because the pre-scan consumes --json as the option value. Fix by sharing one argument scanner between the pre-scan and option resolution. Fold in the review's NIT: ADR 0002's 'produces' sentence still omits uncaught. Filed from the #34 approval; not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: One argument scanner identifies the command token and the --repo value identically for commander and the pre-scan; `glyph --repo --json callers x` and `glyph --repo <dir> --json callers x` choose the same output mode on a success path and a failure path.
Tests cover `--repo --json` on a success path and a failure path, and the `--repo=<dir>` form.
ADR 0002's "produces" sentence names `uncaught` beside usage, not_found and indeterminate.

plan: Add one scanArgv scanner to src/program.ts that models commander: --repo (and --repo=) takes the next token as its value even when it starts with a dash, and it identifies the first command token.
Route the pre-scan decisions, contextOf and the failure output mode through that scanner instead of a second reading of argv.
Cover --repo --json on a success path and a failure path, and --repo=<dir>; amend ADR 0002 produces sentence to name uncaught.
implementationNotes: Proof: CI run 44022396082 on 6c965f9 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity green); bun run check locally green, 77 tests; lore check and lore validate --strict exit 0. Mutation check: restoring the old failure-path expression (program.opts().json or argv.includes(--json)) turns only the new cli test red at its text-on-failure assertion and leaves the other 19 in that file green. The success-path text and both --repo=<dir> envelope assertions stayed green under that mutation, which is the asymmetry the fix removes.

DEC-183 round-1 reviewer verdict on opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 at head 70039a2a1f547ccf6c2684bb3126d55c4b6eac91, reviewer model claude-opus-5-5 (read-only unit, traced against commander 15.0.0; ran nothing). Recorded verbatim:

VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 at 70039a2 (GCLI-13). I traced the code against commander 15.0.0, pinned in package.json:40, in node_modules/commander/lib/command.js. I did not run anything.

Findings:

1. BLOCKING, src/program.ts:180 and :221-229. The scanner skips the token after `--file`, `--depth` and `--ref`, but commander does not. There is no enablePositionalOptions, so the program-level parseOptions runs over the whole argv first (command.js:1760-1907). At that level these three are unknown options. They switch `dest` to `unknown` at command.js:1866-1871 but do not consume the next token, so a following `--repo`, `--json` or `-v` is still taken by the program at command.js:1804-1828. Only `--repo` takes the next token at program level. Three argvs show the effect:
   a. `glyph impact x --ref --repo /dir HEAD`
      - Commander sets repo=/dir, and impact gets `--ref HEAD`. It succeeds.
      - The scanner's `--ref` eats `--repo`, so `scanned.repo` is undefined and contextOf analyzes the cwd. Result: the wrong repository, exit 0.
      - On dev, contextOf read `program.opts().repo` and analyzed /dir. This is a success-path regression, and it contradicts AC0 ("identifies … the --repo value identically for commander and the pre-scan"). The comment at :206-207 ("their value is never a command token or a flag") is wrong about commander.
   b. `glyph callers --file --json src a` (or `impact x --depth --json 3`)
      - Commander sets json=true and file=src, and succeeds.
      - The scanner sees json=false, so the output is text.
      - On dev this was a JSON envelope. Success and failure still agree with each other, but both now disagree with commander.
   c. `glyph --json impact x --depth -v`
      - The scanner's `--depth` eats `-v`, so the JSON version intercept at :458 is skipped.
      - Commander's version listener then prints the version as text to stdout under `--json`.
      - On dev, `argv.includes("-v")` produced the envelope, so this is a contract regression.
   Fix: only `--repo` should consume the next token. Drop `--file`, `--depth` and `--ref` from the skip set. They can still clear onlyKnownGlobals as unknown options, which is what commander does with them. Add a test for (a) at least. The writer's mutation check only touched the failure-path expression, so it could not catch this.

2. NIT, src/program.ts:216-239. The scanner ignores `--` (end of options). After `--`, commander moves every remaining token into operands (command.js:1789-1792), and the subcommand does not re-parse them (command.js:1563-1566). Examples:
   - `glyph callers -- --json` gets a JSON not_found envelope, but commander has json=false.
   - `glyph --json callers -- -v` gets a version envelope with exit 0, where commander would look up a symbol named `-v`.
   This predates the PR (dev's failure path also used argv.includes). Because TS identifiers and git refs cannot start with `-`, it only affects not-found or error paths in practice. Suggested fix: stop reading options at `--`, and take the first bare token after it as commandToken if none is set yet.

3. NIT, existed before this PR. Combined short flags such as `-vh` or `-hv` are unknown to the scanner. Commander splits them (command.js:1831-1848), so `glyph -vh --json` prints the version as text, with no envelope.

4. NIT, a behaviour change reported because you asked; it is not a defect. Argvs where `--repo` takes `--help`, `-h`, `--version` or `-v` as its value now count as a bare invocation:
   - `glyph --repo --help` now prints help with exit 0. On dev, wantsHelp/wantsVersion matched, the argv fell through to commander, and it failed with "(outputHelp)" as a usage error, exit 2.
   - `glyph --json --repo --version` was a version envelope on dev and is now a JSON help envelope.
   - `glyph --repo --json` was a JSON help envelope on dev and is now text help.
   All of these follow the scanner's model of `--repo` and are consistent with `glyph --repo <dir>`. Otherwise bare-invocation behaviour is unchanged: `[]`, `[--json]`, `--repo=` (empty value resolves to the cwd, same as commander), `--repo x`, `--repo` as the last token, and an unknown option all match dev.

What I verified against commander 15's source:
- These shapes agree with commander:
  - `--repo=x` and `--repo x`.
  - `--repo` as the last token: no repo, onlyKnownGlobals=false, commander raises optionMissingArgument, usage error.
  - `--repo --json`: repo is "--json" and json=false in both.
  - `--json` before or after the command: the program consumes it anywhere.
  - Repeated `--repo`: the last one wins in both.
  - `--json=x`: unknown option in both, json=false.
  - `--repo --help` and `--repo --version`: consumed as the value in both. The help option is not in this.options (command.js:2589-2611), but `--repo` is required and consumes it at :1809 anyway.
  - `-h`, `--help` and `--version` interleaved elsewhere.
- There is no short alias for `--repo` or `--json`. The only short flags are `-v` and `-h`.
- Output mode cannot differ between success and failure for the same argv: action handlers (:271/:320/:370/:401/:424), the pre-scan branches and the catch block (:490) all read `scanned.json`.
- No path writes JSON beside text: each branch emits exactly once in one mode, and a CommanderError with exitCode 0 returns without writing. The only text-under-`--json` paths are finding 1c (new) and finding 3 (older).
- The ADR 0002 change is accurate. run() emits `uncaught` at program.ts:501, and errors.ts:5 maps it to 1.
- Nothing else in program.ts changed behaviour. The diff only removes GlobalOptions, rewires contextOf, adds scanArgv, changes the buildProgram signature, and routes run() and the catch block through the scan. The contract test uses buildProgram(scanArgv([])), which is fine.
- The new cli test's assertions are consistent with the code.

What a tree read could not establish:
- I traced the code and did not execute any of it. Findings 1a-c and 2 are derived from commander's source and have not been observed running.
- I did not confirm CI run 44022396082, the 77-test count, the mutation result, or `lore check` / `lore validate --strict`.
- I did not check that node_modules in the main checkout is byte-identical to what CI installs. I read commander 15.0.0 there, matching the exact pin.

Round-1 fix (in the round-2 head). Only --repo consumes the next token now; --file, --depth and --ref are unknown at program level exactly as commander treats them, so 'impact x --ref --repo /dir HEAD' selects /dir again. Options stop at --, and the first token after it names the command if none is set. Combined short flags (-vh, -hv) are split like commander. Five new cli tests cover (a) the --repo-after-a-subcommand-option regression, (b) --json after --file, (c) -v after --depth under --json, the -- terminator both ways, and -vh; all five go red on 70039a2 before the fix and green after it. Nit 4, noted and left as the reviewer asked: a --repo that consumes --help, -h, --version or -v now counts as a bare invocation, so 'glyph --repo --help' prints help with exit 0 (dev raised a usage error), 'glyph --json --repo --version' is a JSON help envelope (dev: version envelope) and 'glyph --repo --json' is text help (dev: JSON help). All follow the scanner model of --repo and match 'glyph --repo <dir>'.

DEC-183 round-2 reviewer verdict on opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 at head 9de47be6318e7a16ee317c7ef11d2ec6fef1d3e9, reviewer model claude-opus-5-5 (read-only unit, traced against commander 15.0.0; ran nothing). Recorded verbatim:

VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 at 9de47be (GCLI-13), DEC-183 round 2. Reviewer model: claude-opus-5-5. I am a read-only unit: I traced the code against commander 15.0.0 in node_modules/commander/lib/command.js and option.js, and ran nothing.

Findings:

1. BLOCKING. The short-cluster model is wrong: src/program.ts:194-209 (combinedShortFlags) and :260-265.
   - At program level, `-v` is the only registered short option. `.version(…, "-v, --version")` registers it through `_registerOption` (command.js:2216).
   - The help option is never in `this.options`. It is built lazily with `createOption` (command.js:2589, 2606-2611).
   - Help detection matches only exact tokens: `helpOption.is(arg)`, which is `short === arg || long === arg` (option.js:243-244, command.js:2702).
   - The cluster branch (command.js:1832-1848) splits a cluster only while its leading short is a known option.
   - So commander's real rule is this. A single-dash token longer than 2 whose second character is `v` emits version. The listener writes the version and exits at command.js:2218-2221, before the rest of the cluster is read. Every other cluster is an unknown option. An `h` inside a cluster never means help.
   The scanner instead sets help or version for any cluster made only of h and v, and returns null for anything else. Each shape against commander:
   a. `glyph -vh --json`: version envelope. Correct, but only by accident: `-v` wins in both models.
   b. `glyph -hv --json`: version envelope, exit 0. Commander treats `-hv` as an unknown option, so this is a usage error, exit 2. Dev agreed with commander: `argv.includes("-v")` was false, onlyKnownGlobalOptions was false, and it went to parse and gave a JSON usage envelope. Without `--json`, `glyph -hv` still gives a usage error, exit 2. So adding `--json` flips the exit code from 2 to 0.
   c. `glyph -hh --json`: JSON help envelope, exit 0. Commander says unknown option. `glyph callers -hh --json` gives the callers manifest, exit 0, where commander and dev give a usage error.
   d. `glyph -vx --json` (also `--json -vx`): the scanner returns null and version stays false. Commander still emits version from the leading `-v`, so the version is printed as text on stdout under `--json`. This predates the PR, but the correct model fixes it for free.
   I am marking this BLOCKING because the round-2 delta introduced it. It changes a frozen exit code under `--json` relative to dev. That is the same standard round 1 applied to its 1c, which was a contract regression against dev.
   Suggested fix: a single-dash token of length > 2 with `arg[1] === "v"` sets version only. Every other cluster is unknown and clears onlyKnownGlobals.
   Tests: the test at test/cli.test.ts:254 (`-vh --json`) passes under both the wrong model and the right one, so it cannot tell them apart. That is likely why the writer's probe "reproduced commander". Add tests that do discriminate: `-hv --json` should give a usage envelope with exit 2, and `-vx --json` should give a version.info envelope.

2. Provenance for finding 1. Round 1's NIT 3 was itself wrong about `-hv`. It said "Commander splits them (command.js:1831-1848)", but line 1833 eats only a known leading short, and `-h` is not one. The writer followed that claim.

3. NIT. The GCLI-13 record is inaccurate: .quest/completed/GCLI-13.json:1.
   - The writer's round-1-fix note says "Combined short flags (-vh, -hv) are split like commander", and the finalSummary says "-vh style clusters split into short flags".
   - Both are false for `-hv`, per finding 1.
   - Append a correcting note with the round-3 fix. Do not edit the verbatim round-1 verdict, which is history.
   - Everything else in the record matches the code: only --repo consumes, `--` ends options, the five tests and their shapes, and nit 4 left as is. The finalSummary citing c80a45d rather than 9de47be is fine, because 9de47be only touches the record.

4. NIT. The `--` handling is right for the case the brief describes. The brief's premise is only conditionally true: src/program.ts:237-245, with the comment at :222-224.
   - The subcommand skips re-parsing the tokens after `--` only when program-level `dest === operands` at that `--` (command.js:1789-1792).
   - If an unknown option or a subcommand's option comes first, commander pushes `--` and the rest into `unknown`. The subcommand then re-parses them: its required option can consume `--` as its value, and `_outputHelpIfRequested(parsed.unknown)` (command.js:1597) finds a `--help` after the `--`.
   - Two shapes: `glyph --json callers --bogus -- --help` and `glyph --json callers --file -- --help`. Both print text help under `--json`, exit 0. Dev's `wantsHelp` gave a JSON manifest.
   - This is a text-under-`--json` regression against dev, but it needs either an unknown option or `--file` swallowing `--`. I rate it NIT. Re-weigh it if you like.
   - Every shape without a preceding unknown or value option matches commander. That includes the two tests at test/cli.test.ts:237.

5. NIT, optional. A lone `-` is an operand to commander, because `maybeOption` needs length > 1 (command.js:1765-1767). The scanner never takes `-` as commandToken. So in `glyph - callers --help --json` the scanner picks `callers` and returns its manifest, where commander would show program help. Execution paths are unaffected, because commander still fails on unknown command '-'.

What I verified against commander 15's source:
- All round-1 shapes now agree with commander:
  - `impact x --ref --repo /dir HEAD`: repo=/dir. `--ref` is unknown at program level, and impact gets `--ref HEAD`.
  - `callers --file --json src a` and `impact x --depth --json 3`: json=true.
  - `--json impact x --depth -v`: version=true, so the JSON intercept gives an envelope.
- `--repo -- x`: both take `--` as the value. The skip consumes it before the `--` check can fire, so a following `--json` stays a flag, which commander also does.
- `--` as the very first token:
  - `-- callers x`: commander puts both into operands and dispatches callers. The scanner's commandToken is callers.
  - `-- --json`: both give unknown command '--json', in text.
  - `--json -- -v`: both give a JSON usage envelope.
  - `glyph --` alone is treated as a bare invocation and gives help, exit 0. Commander itself would call help({error:true}), but this matches how the pre-scan already handles a plain `glyph`, so it is consistent.
- These also agree: `--repo=--json`, `--json=x` (unknown in both), `--depth=-v` (unknown at program level in both), negative-number tokens (unknown, never a command token), `--repo` as the last token (optionMissingArgument, usage), `--repo=` empty (resolves to the cwd in both), repeated `--repo` (last one wins).
- Output mode agrees between the success and failure paths for every fixed argv:
  - Every action handler reads contextOf(scanned).json.
  - The pre-scan branches read scanned.json.
  - The catch block reads scanned.json (:519).
- Nothing writes JSON beside text. Every branch emits once in one mode, and a CommanderError with exitCode 0 returns without writing (:521).
- The remaining text-under-`--json` paths are commander's own writes when the scanner misreads a shape: finding 1d, and finding 4's help.
- The five new tests are consistent with the code. Each would be red on 70039a2 for the reason the record gives.

What a tree read could not establish:
- I executed nothing. Findings 1, 4 and 5 are derived from commander's source and have not been observed running.
- I did not confirm CI run 44024214414, the count of 82 tests (consistent with 77+5), the red-on-70039a2 and green-now results, or the writer's local probe.
- I did not check that the main checkout's node_modules is byte-identical to what CI installs. I read commander 15.0.0 there, matching the pin.

Correction to this record (round 3). The round-1-fix note and the 9de47be final summary both claimed combined short flags '-vh, -hv' are split like commander. That is false for -hv: commander registers -v but not -h as a program option, splits a cluster only while its leading short is known, and matches help only as an exact token. Measured against commander 15.0.0: -vh and -vx emit version; -hv and -hh are unknown options, a usage error with exit 2. The two verbatim verdicts above are history and are left untouched.

Round-2 fix (in the round-3 head). clusterIsVersion is now commander's real rule: a single-dash token longer than two characters whose second character is v sets version only, and every other cluster is an unknown option that clears onlyKnownGlobals. So -vh and -vx answer a version envelope under --json, while -hv and -hh give a usage envelope at exit 2 (they were version/help envelopes at exit 0 on 9de47be, a frozen-exit-code regression against dev). The discriminating test covers -vx, -hv and -hh; on 9de47be the -vx case printed text and both clusters exited 0, all three now match commander. Nit 4 (a -- after an unknown or value option) and nit 5 (a lone -) are filed as GCLI-28.

DEC-183 round-3 reviewer verdict on opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 at head 018116405f24d73ec8c6cc15a93a21e9c092f45d, reviewer model claude-opus-5-5 (read-only unit, scoped to 9de47be..0181164, traced against commander 15.0.0; ran nothing). Recorded verbatim:

VERDICT: APPROVE

opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 at 0181164 (GCLI-13), DEC-183 round 3, scoped to the delta 9de47be..0181164. Reviewer model: claude-opus-5-5. I am a read-only unit. I traced the code against commander 15.0.0 in the main checkout's node_modules/commander/lib/command.js and option.js, and ran nothing.

Findings:

1. NIT, test/cli.test.ts:274. The older test, "combined short flags such as -vh take the version under --json", still passes under both the round-2 model and the round-3 model. That makes it a positive control, not a discriminator. Keeping it is fine. Its name still describes the round-2 framing ("combined short flags"). Optional: rename it, or fold it into the new test at :254.

There are no BLOCKING findings.

What I verified against commander's source:

- clusterIsVersion (src/program.ts:206-208) matches commander's rule exactly.
  - Commander's cluster branch is command.js:1832-1848: `arg.length > 2 && arg[0]==='-' && arg[1]!=='-'`, then `_findOption('-'+arg[1])`.
  - `_findOption` searches only `this.options` (:1676-1677), and matches on `short===arg || long===arg` (option.js:243-244).
  - At program level the only registered short is `-v`, from `.version(…, "-v, --version")` at program.ts:285 and command.js:2216. `--repo` and `--json` have no short. The subcommand options `--file`, `--depth`, `--all` and `--ref` have no short either.
  - The help option is created lazily (:2589-2611) and is never pushed into `options`. Help is detected only as an exact token (:2702).
  - `-v` is boolean. Its listener writes the version and calls `_exit(0)` (:2218-2221), which throws under exitOverride before activeGroup is read again.
  - Shape by shape, with the scanner matching commander in every case:
    - `-v` alone is caught first by GLOBAL_FLAGS (:254), so it never reaches the cluster rule.
    - `-vv`, `-vh`, `-vx`, `-v1`, `-v=` and `-v=x` are version. For `-v=x`, the earlier `_findOption('-v=x')` at :1805 misses, the cluster branch takes `-v`, and the scanner's `equals` applies only to `--` tokens, so it reaches clusterIsVersion.
    - `-hv`, `-hh`, `-1v`, `-12` and `-Vx` are unknown and clear onlyKnownGlobals at :264. They never become commandToken, because they start with `-`.
    - `-V` (length 2) is not a cluster in either model, and is unknown in both. The existing test at :594 covers it.
    - `--v` and `--vx` start with `--`, so they are not clusters in either model and are unknown in both.
- The unknown-cluster path matches commander's output mode and exit code.
  - `-hv --json` and `-hh --json`: json=true, help=false, version=false, onlyKnownGlobals=false. So none of the pre-scan branches at :485-510 fire, and the argv goes to parseAsync.
  - In commander, `-hv` goes to `unknown`, and `--json` is still consumed as a known option. In `_parseCommand` the args are non-empty, so the help({error}) at :1587-1595 is skipped. `_outputHelpIfRequested(['-hv'])` is false. With no operands, :1644-1645 calls `checkForUnknownOptions` → `unknownOption`, exit 1.
  - The catch block at :518-522 turns that into a JSON usage envelope on stderr, empty stdout, exit 2.
  - Without `--json` it is the same error as text, exit 2.
  - `callers -hh --json` reaches the callers action's `checkForUnknownOptions` (:1610). That is now a usage error, exit 2. On 9de47be it was the manifest, exit 0.
- The new test discriminates the two models (test/cli.test.ts:254-272). Under 9de47be's combinedShortFlags:
  - `-vx` returned null, so the argv went to commander. The version printed as plain text, and `JSON.parse(stdout)` would throw.
  - `-hv` gave a version envelope with exit 0, which fails `code === 2`.
  - `-hh` gave a help envelope with exit 0, which also fails.
  - All three go green under the round-3 rule.
- No round-1 or round-2 fixed shape regressed. The delta changes only the cluster branch (:260-263), the two comments, and the removal of combinedShortFlags. `--repo` consumption, the `--` terminator, the unknown subcommand value options, and `-v` after `--depth` are byte-unchanged. Their tests at :205-251 are present and unchanged. `-vh --json` still sets version.
- The record is accurate.
  - The round-1 verbatim verdict is byte-identical between the old and new lines of .quest/completed/GCLI-13.json.
  - The round-1-fix note is left as it was, and the appended correction names its false "-hv" claim and states commander's real rule, as round 2 asked.
  - The round-3 fix note's before/after claims match my trace of 9de47be: `-vx` text, `-hv` and `-hh` exit 0.
  - finalSummary no longer claims clusters split.
- GCLI-28 (.quest/tasks/GCLI-28.json) files round-2 nits 4 and 5 faithfully, with matching shapes and acceptance criteria.

What a tree read could not establish:
- I executed nothing. Every behaviour above is traced from source. I did not observe any of it, including the writer's measured `commander.version` and `commander.unknownOption` codes. My trace agrees with them.
- The round-2 verbatim verdict was added in this delta. I had no copy of the message round 2 actually sent, so I could not confirm the recorded text is byte-identical to it. It reads consistently with the brief's summary of round 2.
- I did not confirm CI run 44026084021, the 83-test count (consistent with 82 + 1), that the new test is red on 9de47be, or lore check / validate. I also did not confirm that the main checkout's node_modules is byte-identical to what CI installs. I read commander 15.0.0 there, matching the pin.
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 (round 3, commit 6757dd4): scanArgv is the one reader of the global vocabulary and, after two review rounds, matches commander's measured rules. Only --repo consumes its next token; --file/--depth/--ref are unknown at program level and consume nothing; options stop at --; and a short cluster means version only when its second character is v (-vh, -vx are version; -hv, -hh are unknown options, usage at exit 2). contextOf, the help/version pre-parse and the failure output mode all read that one scan, so success and failure cannot disagree, and ADR 0002 produces names uncaught. Validated by CI run 44026084021 on 6757dd4 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity green); bun run check green, 83 tests; lore check and lore validate --strict green. Round-1 and round-2 verdicts are on this record verbatim, the round-3 correction of the -hv claim is appended, and nits 4-5 are GCLI-28.
